title: Deterministic atom-shuttle interconnects via ultrafast atom-ion entangling gate
abstract: Neutral-atom arrays and trapped-ion crystals offer complementary strengths for fault-tolerant quantum computing but lack a fast way to deterministically interact. Here we propose a controlled-$Z$ gate generated by the charge-induced-dipole ($C_4$) force between a Rydberg-excited atom and a trapped ion, balanced by a spin-dependent optical Magnus force on the ion that closes phase-space trajectories within a few microseconds. Toggling the Rydberg state extends the scheme to multi-ion crystals at negligible overhead. The resulting ${\sim}5\,$kHz atom shuttle accelerates short-distance QCCD links and enables hybrid qLDPC memories in which atom logical qubits are written onto an ion block treated as a passive storage zone. We perform circuit-level Monte Carlo simulations and find that the hybrid architecture supports orders of magnitude more operations than atom-only or ion-only architectures at fixed code distance and logical error rate.
summary: The paper presents a breakthrough method to deterministically link neutral-atom arrays and trapped-ion crystals using ultrafast atom shuttling ($\sim 5 	ext{ kHz}$) and microsecond $	ext{CZ}$ gates. By leveraging the charge-induced-dipole force, they demonstrate a hybrid quantum architecture that significantly boosts computational power and offers superior long-term storage capabilities compared to single-platform systems.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing a fast, deterministic method to enable reliable quantum entanglement and interconnectivity between two leading platforms: neutral-atom arrays and trapped-ion crystals.
main_result: The authors propose a hybrid architecture using ultrafast atom shuttling ($\sim 5 	ext{ kHz}$) combined with microsecond $	ext{CZ}$ gates, which significantly outperforms single-platform approaches for scaling quantum computation.
method: The core mechanism involves generating a controlled-$Z$ gate via the charge–induced-dipole ($	ext{C}4$) force between a Rydberg atom and a trapped ion, modulated by a spin-dependent optical Magnus force to close phase-space trajectories rapidly.
model_or_system: The system combines neutral atoms in optical tweezers with trapped ions. The gate relies on the $	ext{C}4$ interaction Hamiltonian, which is controlled by toggling Rydberg states or using circular Rydberg states for enhanced coherence and sign control of the force.
key_observables: Gate time ($\sim \mu	ext{s}$), Interconnect rate ($\sim 5 	ext{ kHz}$), Logical error rates ($p_T$), and Fidelity ($F$).
important_parameters: Rydberg state parameters (e.g., $n=60, 80$), $	ext{C}4$ coupling strength, detuning ($\delta_d$), and separation distance ($L \le 2 	ext{ mm}$).
main_assumptions: The ion block can act as a passive storage zone for hybrid memory schemes; the gate fidelity is limited by Rydberg decay or technical noise sources.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase-space trajectories showing distinct closed loops for $	ext{CZ}$ gates, and comparative plots show that atom shuttling dominates interconnect rates up to $2 	ext{ mm}$, while error scaling shows hybrid memory improving with algorithm length.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the need for fast interconnects. It then details the microsecond $	ext{CZ}$ gate mechanism using $	ext{C}4$ and Magnus forces, followed by demonstrating its application to high-rate atom shuttling and a superior hybrid quantum memory architecture compared to pure-platform methods.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the physical bottleneck of connecting disparate quantum hardware modules. The use of Rydberg physics (specifically circular states) combined with ion trapping dynamics provides an advanced, scalable protocol for realizing high-fidelity quantum interconnects.
